topic.subject: social
topic.title: Gender, religion and caste in politics
topic.scope: gender division, women's representation, communalism, secular state, caste in politics

misconceptions.statement: The division of labor between men and women is biologically determined and natural.
misconceptions.why: Students often observe traditional household roles in their own families and assume these are innate rather than socially constructed.
misconceptions.fix: Gender roles are social constructs created by society, not biological necessities; they vary across cultures and time.

probe.question: Why do women mostly perform domestic chores like cooking and cleaning?
probe.wrong_answer: Because women are naturally born with the instinct and physical ability to do housework better than men.

misconceptions.statement: Increasing the number of women in parliament will automatically solve all problems faced by women.
misconceptions.why: Students often believe that identity alone guarantees specific policy outcomes without considering political ideologies.
misconceptions.fix: While representation is important, political parties and their ideologies also dictate how issues are addressed, regardless of the gender of the representative.

probe.question: If 50% of MPs are women, will all gender-based discrimination disappear?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, because women representatives will naturally prioritize and solve all women's issues.

misconceptions.statement: A secular state is one that is against all religions.
misconceptions.why: Students often confuse 'secularism' with 'atheism' due to common misconceptions in popular media.
misconceptions.fix: A secular state does not favor any religion but treats all religions with equal respect and provides no official status to any single faith.

probe.question: Does a secular government allow religious festivals to be celebrated?
probe.wrong_answer: No, because a secular government must ban all religious activities to remain neutral.

concepts.name: Caste in Politics and Politics in Caste

misconceptions.statement: Caste is the only factor that determines how people vote in India.
misconceptions.why: Media coverage of 'vote banks' often oversimplifies complex electoral behavior into single-factor explanations.
misconceptions.fix: Caste is one of many factors influencing voting; economic development, party performance, and individual candidate appeal also play significant roles.

probe.question: Why do political parties choose candidates from specific castes in a constituency?
probe.wrong_answer: Because voters only care about their own caste and will never vote for anyone else.
